title: SPA/189/2019 of MAN SINGH SAINI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 189 of 2019
With
Delay Condonation Application No. 3228 of 2019
Man Singh Saini ...Appellant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and others ...Respondents
Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel for the appellant.
Mr. S.S. Chaudhary, learned Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand-respondent
no. 1.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, learned counsel for respondent no.3.
Mr. Navneet Kaushik, learned counsel for respondent no. 5.
Dated: 28th March, 2019
Coram: Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
 Hon'ble N.S. Dhanik, J.
Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J. (Oral)
 The application seeking condonation of the delay of 58 days in
preferring the appeal is not opposed by Mr. Navneet Kaushik, learned
counsel for the respondent-writ petitioner and the delay is, therefore,
condoned.
2. Heard Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel for the appellant-fourth respondent and Mr. Navneet Kaushik, learned counsel for the
respondent-writ petitioner and, with their consent, the special appeal
is disposed of at the stage of admission.
3. The appellant herein was arrayed in the writ petition eo nomine
as the fourth respondent. The dispute in the writ petition relates to
correction of the final list of delimitation of constituencies of the
Cooperative Society after the said list was published. These
corrections were, admittedly, carried out by the appellant-fourth
respondent, who was arrayed eo nomine as the fourth respondent in
the writ petition.

2
4. In the order under appeal, the learned Single Judge has
observed that, when asked to show the provision of law under which
he had effected corrections, the learned counsel for the appellant-fourth respondent was unable to show any such provision, conferring
on the appellant-fourth respondent, the power to make corrections
after the final list of delimitation of constituencies had been published.
It is, in such circumstances, that the learned Single Judge observed
that the election officer must abide strictly by the Rules, and that
elections be notified as per the final order dated 18.08.2018. The
learned Single Judge, thereafter, directed the Secretary, Cooperative,
Government of Uttarakhand, to issue a show cause notice to the
appellant-fourth respondent, seek his explanation and, thereafter, take
appropriate steps, if required.
 5. We do not see how the aforesaid observations in the order
under appeal cause prejudice to the appellant-fourth respondent. The
learned Single Judge has only directed the Secretary, Cooperative,
Government of Uttarakhand to put the appellant-fourth respondent on
notice regarding his act of correcting the list of delimitation of
constituencies after it was published, to then seek his explanation and,
thereafter, take appropriate steps, "if required". It is evident
therefrom that if the authority is satisfied, on the basis of the
explanation submitted by the appellant-fourth respondent, that there
was no error on his part, then the order under appeal does not obligate
the Secretary to impose any punishment on the appellant-fourth
respondent.
6. We see no reason, therefore, to interfere with the order under
appeal. The appeal fails and is, accordingly, dismissed.
7. No costs.
 (N.S. Dhanik, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.)
 28.03.2019 28.03.2019
Rahul
